minimum_next_evidence: Separate wall/controller-self-CPU across profile validation, agent, queues, spawn/postexec, I/O, response verification, JSON and audit; keep original protocol/gates/zero-retry/custody.
Treat existing sampled descendant CPU as incomplete diagnostics and remote CPU as outside the controller numerator.
If retained verification/sync work dominates controller CPU, do not predict a throughput shift from remote helper startup reduction alone.
recommendation: Record the two micro-candidates; do not open another full qualification solely for them without material absolute-cost evidence. Keep R35 on its already planned original qualification. Investigate persistent observation framing only as a separate structural project after phase-cost attribution.

structural_direction.amortization_model: For one explicitly defined metric, potential savings = F*(1-1/k)-E; fixed worker startup cost F, requests per generation k, added per-request framing cost E.
structural_direction.batch_alternative: A new same-host job batch can amortize startup, but must specify each item identity/deadline/audit/output/partial-failure contract. It does not improve callers that still issue single requests; internal microbatch also needs fairness and per-logical-request admission proofs.

existing_related_not_drop_in.facts: Controller-local cooperative FD handoff broker; daemon intentionally independent of MCP lifetime; Rust invoke still creates Python per call. Not a cross-host durable-job observation protocol.
Explicit same-host 1..16 file batch with per-file checks/shared byte ceiling and no cross-file atomic snapshot; uses one run_python_json for a batch. Not a job status/read batch.
